However, the decrypted payload (loaded via the obfuscated code in index.min.js) is the well-known event-stream/copay attack which exfiltrates Bitcoin wallet data. dimensions.name: obfuscation
dimensions.label: Obfuscation / encoding patterns (base64, eval, dynamic require)
dimensions.reasoning: index.min.js has a new IIFE appended that uses hex-encoded strings to hide all meaningful identifiers. Buffer.from(r,'hex').toString() is used to decode strings like '2e2f746573742f64617461' (./test/data.js), '63727970746f' (crypto), '6372656174654465636970686572' (createDecipher), '5f636f6d70696c65' (_compile). The data.js file contains two massive hex-encoded blobs (encrypted ciphertext). The code decrypts one blob using crypto.createDecipher('aes256', npm_package_description), compiles and executes the result via module.constructor._compile — a classic multi-layer obfuscation and dynamic code execution pattern.

This is explicitly conditioned on the presence of a specific environment variable — the payload only runs when the consuming package (Copay wallet) sets that env var, making it a targeted supply chain attack gated on the victim's environment.

llm_summary: This is the infamous event-stream/flatmap-stream supply chain attack (CVE-2018-16462). The 0.1.1 update appends a self-executing IIFE to index.min.js that uses hex-encoded strings to obfuscate all meaningful identifiers, loads encrypted payload data from test/data.js, decrypts it using the consuming package's npm_package_description environment variable as an AES-256 key, then dynamically compiles and executes the result via module.constructor._compile. The attack is highly targeted (only activates in the Copay Bitcoin wallet environment), uses multiple layers of obfuscation, and executes at require-time. This is a definitive, confirmed malicious package update with the highest possible risk score.
